questions.text: Reproductive health is a holistic concept encompassing physical, emotional, and social well-being. Describe any four essential components of a national programme aimed at creating a reproductively healthy society, drawing from the various action plans and support systems mentioned for our country.
Explain why reproductive health education, focusing on safe sexual practices and STI awareness, is particularly crucial for adolescents. How does it contribute to a socially responsible society?

Apart from creating awareness, what are the two broad aspects of support a Reproductive and Child Health Care programme provides to tackle reproduction-related problems? Give one example for each aspect.
The implementation of better strategies is necessary for efficient reproductive healthcare. Justify this statement with reference to the statutory ban on amniocentesis for sex-determination.
Why is it important to educate fertile couples and people of marriageable age group about birth control options, as mentioned in the text? Explain one related reason.
What is the primary step towards achieving a reproductively healthy society, as emphasized in the national action plans?

options.a: Providing advanced surgical facilities for infertility treatments
options.c: Counseling and creating awareness about reproductive health and STIs
options.d: Mandating institutional delivery for all pregnancies

questions.text: Study the diagram below showing two scenarios. Scenario A depicts a society with high awareness campaigns on safe sexual practices, while Scenario B shows one without such programs. Which conclusion can be best drawn regarding Scenario A?
questions.image_prompt: A split diagram. Left side (Scenario A) shows a group of diverse young adults looking at informative posters about STIs and contraception, with a low, flat line graph labeled 'STI Incidence'. Right side (Scenario B) shows a similar group in a dim setting, looking confused, with a steeply rising line graph labeled 'STI Incidence'.

options.a: It leads to a higher rate of medical termination of pregnancy.
options.b: It is ineffective without mandatory immunization programs.
options.c: It contributes to building a socially responsible and healthy society.
options.d: It increases the need for statutory bans on diagnostic techniques.

questions.text: A couple is seeking guidance under the Reproductive and Child Health Care programme. Which of the following would NOT be considered a core aspect of medical care provided to them?

options.c: Postnatal care for the mother and child
options.d: Financial planning for the child's education

questions.text: The implementation of better techniques and new strategies in reproductive health care is primarily aimed at:

options.a: Reducing the cost of all medical procedures.
options.b: Providing more efficient care and assistance to people.
options.c: Focusing solely on adolescent health problems.
options.d: Replacing all traditional methods of birth control.

questions.text: Statutory ban on amniocentesis for sex-determination is a program that merits attention because it aims to:

options.a: Promote the use of advanced genetic screening technologies.
options.b: Increase the overall rate of prenatal diagnostic procedures.
options.c: Legally check the increasing menace of female foeticide.
options.d: Ensure mandatory sex determination for all pregnancies.

questions.text: Which of the following is a combination of infrastructural needs for the successful implementation of reproductive health action plans?

options.a: Professional expertise, material support, and legal frameworks only.
options.b: Strong infrastructural facilities, professional expertise, and material support.
options.c: Mass media campaigns and statutory bans only.
options.d: Adolescent education programs and immunization drives only.

questions.text: Educating people in the marriageable age group about available birth control options primarily addresses which aspect of the Reproductive and Child Health Care programme?

options.c: Care of pregnant mothers and postnatal management.
options.d: Planning and spacing of pregnancies for maternal and child health.

questions.text: Massive child immunization programs are highlighted as a merit because they:

options.a: Directly reduce the incidence of sexually transmitted diseases.
options.b: Are a key component of building a reproductively healthy society.
options.c: Replace the need for antenatal care for the mother.
options.d: Focus solely on the physical health of adolescents.

questions.text: A 'reproductively healthy society' as described in the text encompasses well-being in:

options.a: Only the physical and emotional aspects of reproduction.
options.b: Physical, emotional, behavioural, and social aspects of reproduction.
options.c: The economic and educational status of individuals.
options.d: The legal and political frameworks governing reproduction.
